title: Invariant-Stratified Propagation for Expressive Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Graph neural networks have limited expressivity and struggle to capture structural heterogeneity; standard message-passing architectures cannot distinguish graphs beyond degree sequences and aggregate neighbor information uniformly.

gap.claim: Existing higher-expressivity methods have prohibitive computational costs and lack a unified framework for flexibly encoding diverse structural properties.

contributions.claim: Introduces Invariant-Stratified Propagation, comprising the ISP-WL variant and the ISP-GNN implementation.
Stratifies nodes by graph invariants and processes them hierarchically to encode structural heterogeneity and distinguish nodes with different structural roles in higher-order patterns.
Provides theoretical analysis of expressivity beyond 1-WL, convergence guarantees, and resistance to oversmoothing.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present ISP as a new framework with a novel WL variant and an efficient neural network implementation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report consistent improvements over standard architectures and state-of-the-art expressive baselines across graph classification, node classification, and influence estimation.
The authors report that source code is available.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs face expressivity and structural-heterogeneity limitations.
Higher-expressivity approaches may be computationally costly and lack a unified encoding framework.
The paper introduces ISP, including ISP-WL and ISP-GNN.
ISP uses invariant-based hierarchical strata to encode structural roles and heterogeneity.
The paper reports theoretical guarantees and empirical improvements across three task types.

source_observation.claim: The method processes nodes in hierarchical strata defined by graph invariants.

interpretation.claim: Explicitly representing structural roles may help models distinguish higher-order interactions that uniform aggregation obscures.

application.claim: For graph tasks involving heterogeneous structural roles, consider invariant-aware or hierarchical propagation mechanisms.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which graph families, invariant choices, or task conditions limit the approach.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the graph invariants used or the computational costs of ISP.
The abstract does not provide dataset names, numerical results, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not detail the convergence guarantees or oversmoothing analysis.
